gui.gtcalcboard.guide.basics_desc:
### Canvas Navigation & Zooming
- [Right-Click / Middle-Click Drag]: Freely pan and move the canvas.
- [Scroll Mouse Wheel]: Smoothly zoom in/out between 0.2x and 3.0x.
- Top [⊕ Center] Button: Reset viewport back to origin.

### Adding Recipes to the Board
1. In the EMI item list, hover over any item and press [R] (Recipes) or [U] (Uses).
2. Click the [+] button on the recipe screen to immediately place the machine node onto the board.
3. Alternatively, click the top [➕ Add] button to search and pick recipes directly from the search dialog.

> ★ TIP: Resize Cards: Drag the bottom-right corner [◢] of any machine card to freely expand its size.
gui.gtcalcboard.guide.search_desc:
### Contextual Drag-to-Search & Auto-Wire
- [Drag Port to Empty Canvas]: Drag a wire from any output port (or input port) and release on empty canvas to open the Recipe Search dialog pre-filtered for matching consumers (or producers).
- Selecting a recipe immediately spawns the machine node at your cursor and [automatically connects the wire]!
- Hold [Shift] while selecting to automatically solve and match machine counts 1:1.

### Advanced Parametric Search Engine
- [Input material filter]: `in:iron`, `input:steam`, or `>iron` (filters recipes consuming this item/fluid).
- [Output product filter]: `out:steel`, `output:oxygen`, or `<steel` (filters recipes producing this item/fluid).
- [Compound filtering]: `in:iron out:steel` (recipes consuming Iron and producing Steel).
- Multi-token [AND] matching: Space or '&' (e.g. `pyrolyse oil` matches recipes with both terms).
- [OR] matching: '|' (e.g. `oil | creosote` matches either item).
- [NOT] exclusion: '!' (e.g. `!in:water`, `!out:slag`, `pyrolyse !charcoal`).
- Mod prefix: `@gtceu` or `@minecraft` (or `in:@gtceu`, `out:@thermal`).
- Item / Fluid tags: `#forge:logs` or `#c:dusts` (or `in:#forge:dusts`).
- Machine category: `[pyrolyse_oven]` or `[chemical_reactor]`.
- Exact quotes: `"sulfuric acid"` or `in:"heavy fuel"`.

### Singleplayer Pause Control
- Click the toolbar [⏸ Pause: ON] / [▶ Pause: OFF] button to decide whether to freeze singleplayer while calculating complex lines.
gui.gtcalcboard.guide.wiring_title: ⚡ Chapter 3. Wiring & Shift-Drag Auto Ratio Matching
gui.gtcalcboard.guide.wiring_desc:
### Basic Wire Connections
- Left-click the [Green Output Port] on a supplier machine, then left-click the [Blue Input Port] on a consumer machine to create a fluid/item connection wire.

### ✨ Shift + Drag Wire Connection (Auto Ratio)
- Hold down [Shift] while connecting an output port to an input port!
- The board will instantly analyze supplier production vs consumer consumption and [automatically calculate & scale the consumer machine count] so production and consumption match 1:1.
- Example: Connect a Chemical Reactor producing 500 mB/s to a Distillation Tower consuming 100 mB/s with Shift -> Distillation Tower count becomes [5.0 machines] automatically!

### ↔ Junction Nodes & Estimated Time (ET / DT)
- [Double-Click Wire]: Inserts a zero-cost Reroute Junction Node to split and organize complex wiring.
- [Left-Click Badge]: Click the bottom badge to enter a Target Batch quantity (e.g. 64 items, 10,000 mB). The board calculates real-time Estimated Completion Time (ET: xx.xs) based on net inflow rate.
- [Raw Inflow DT]: For raw input junctions with no upstream supplier, it calculates stock Depletion Time (DT: xx.xs) based on consumption rate.
- [Right-Click Junction]: Open supply dialog to configure Infinite Supply (∞) or Fixed Throughput (items/s, mB/s) to isolate upstream supply lines.
- [Shift + Right-Click]: Reset target batch quantity back to 0.

### Disconnecting Wires
- [Right-click] directly on any wire curve or right-click any connected port to sever the connection.
gui.gtcalcboard.guide.master_title: ⌖ Chapter 4. Base Master Anchor & Auto Ratio
gui.gtcalcboard.guide.master_desc:
### Base Master Anchor Recipe
- In a multi-step production line, click the [⌖] button on the top-right of your final target product machine.
- The machine card will glow [Golden] and serve as the fixed anchor for the entire flowchart.

### Automation Toolbar Tools
- [⚖ Auto Ratio (Ratio)]: Scales and balances all upstream supplier machines backwards throughout the entire line to match the Master Anchor's exact requirement.
- [⚡ Auto Connect (Connect)]: Automatically scans all nodes on the canvas and wires matching item/fluid ports.
- [▲ Max Flow (Flow)]: Overclocks all nodes to MAX tier and optimizes parallel hatches to compact huge lines into single high-throughput units.

> ★ TIP: Click [Tier], [STD/PERF OC], [/2], or [x2] on any card to test individual overclocking and parallel efficiency.
gui.gtcalcboard.guide.module_desc:
### What is a Compound Module?
- A feature that condenses dozens of interconnected chemical reactors, distillation towers, and centrifuges into a [Single Compound Module Card] using [Ctrl + Shift + G].
- [Ctrl + G]: Creates an enclosing Visual Frame around selected nodes.
- [Ctrl + Shift + S]: Groups selected nodes into a Shared Machine Pool frame, computing total duty (%) and required physical machines (Ceil) with hardware sync.

### Key Benefits of Modularization
1. [Automatic Byproduct Encapsulation]: 100% self-recycled and internally consumed intermediate fluids/items are hidden, exposing only [Raw External Inputs] and [Net Final Outputs].
2. [Proportional Scaling]: Increasing the module card count (e.g. from 1 to 2 or 4) proportionally scales all internal facilities.
3. [Accurate Summary Stats]: Total contained machines (e.g. 58 machines) and power generation/consumption are properly aggregated in the Summary Overlay.

### [⤢ Expand] Instant Restoration
- Click the [⤢] button on the top-right of a module card at any time to restore all individual machines and internal wires onto the canvas.
gui.gtcalcboard.guide.team_title: ▪ Chapter 6. Multiplayer Team Workspaces & Live Collaboration
gui.gtcalcboard.guide.team_desc:
### Real-Time Team Flowcharts
- On dedicated servers with GregTech Calculator Board installed, team members share live flowchart workspaces with real-time synchronization.
- Seamlessly integrates with [FTB Teams], [Phoenix Guilds], and vanilla scoreboard teams.

### Personal Board vs Team Workspace
- [▪ Personal Board] Tab: Your private calculation workspace. Completely local and private.
- [▪ Team Workspace] Tabs: Shared team boards synchronized in real time with all teammates.
- [» Export to Team]: Open a personal tab and click [Export to Team] in the top toolbar to publish your design to the team workspace!

### Smart Edit Locks & Teammate Presence
- Interacting with any node on a team page [automatically acquires a temporary edit lock], preventing simultaneous edit conflicts.
- Active teammates viewing or editing the current page are displayed in the top presence bar.

### Frictionless Auto-Sync & Save History
- Changes auto-save in the background (3-second inactivity debounce and screen exit).
- Click [~ Saves] to browse past revision logs and [Copy to Me] to fork past team versions into your personal board.
gui.gtcalcboard.guide.pages_title: ▪ Chapter 7. Multi-Page Tabs, Folder Browser & Blueprints
gui.gtcalcboard.guide.pages_desc:
### Top Page Tab Bar (Presets)
- Organize your builds into separate, independent flowcharts via the top tab bar.
- [+] Button: Create a new blank board page.
- [Click Tab]: Instantly switch pages (remembers camera pan & zoom per page).
- [Right-Click Tab]: Rename the tab inline.
- [x Button]: Remove unwanted tabs.

### Hierarchical Page Browser Drawer
- [≡ Button / Tab]: Open the left folder browser drawer to organize dozens of pages into nested subfolders.
- [Ctrl + K / P]: Open the Quick Page Switcher to instantly find and switch between pages.
- [≡+ New Folder]: Create new root folders and nested subfolders.
- [Ctrl / Shift + Click]: Select multiple pages and folders just like Windows Explorer.
- [Drag & Drop]: Drag selected pages or folders into any folder or back to root.

### AE2 Autocrafting Processing Pattern Binding
- [◆ Bind AE2 Pattern]: Bind a page directly to an AE2 Processing Pattern to calculate exact ETA and detect bottleneck stages during ME autocrafting.

### Folder Blueprints & Disk Storage
- [» Export Folder]: Right-click a folder to export all sub-pages into a [Folder Blueprint Code (GTFOLDER:...)] or save to disk (*.gtcb).
- [« Import Folder / ≡ Disk Files]: Restore full folder hierarchies and page flowcharts in 1 click from clipboard or saved disk files.

> ★ TIP: Your progress is automatically preserved even if you exit Minecraft!
gui.gtcalcboard.guide.shortcuts_title: ▪ Chapter 8. Marquee Box Selection, Clipboard, & Renaming
gui.gtcalcboard.guide.shortcuts_desc:
### Marquee Box Multi-Selection
- [Left-Click & Drag]: Draw a selection box on empty canvas to select multiple machines at once.
- [Shift + Left-Click]: Toggle individual machines into or out of selection.
- [Batch Dragging]: Dragging any selected machine moves all selected machines together while preserving internal wires.

### Grid Snap, Junctions & Flow Modeling
- [G Key]: Toggle 16px precision grid snapping to align nodes, frames, and notes cleanly.
- [Left-Click Junction Badge]: Set target batch quantity for real-time Estimated Time (ET/DT) calculation.
- [Right-Click Junction]: Configure infinite supply (∞) or fixed rate throughput (items/s, mB/s) to block upstream demand propagation.
- [Shift + Right-Click Junction]: Reset target batch quantity back to 0.
- [Machine Hardware Cloner]: Save tier/parallel/addon configs into named templates and batch-inject across nodes.

### Undo, Redo, & Shortcuts
- [Ctrl + Z]: Undo the last action (moving nodes, adding/deleting, connecting wires, grouping, property edits).
- [Ctrl + Y / Ctrl + Shift + Z]: Redo the previously undone action.
- [Ctrl + K / P]: Open the Quick Page Switcher to jump between pages.
- [Ctrl + X]: Cut selected machines and internal wires.
- [Ctrl + C]: Copy selected machines and internal wires to clipboard.
- [Ctrl + V]: Paste duplicated machines at mouse cursor position with new UUIDs.
- [Ctrl + D]: Duplicate selected machines instantly.
- [Delete / Backspace]: Delete selected machines and connections.
- [Ctrl + A]: Select all machines on the canvas.

### Inline Title Renaming
- [Double-Click] any machine header title to open the inline text editor.
- Type your custom name (e.g. [Sulfuric Acid Line 1], [Turbine Generator]) and press [Enter] to save.

gui.gtcalcboard.tutorial.step1_desc: [Right-Click] empty canvas space and select [+ Add Recipe...], or click the top [🔍 Search recipes...] button (or press Space) to place a recipe node (e.g. Boiler).
gui.gtcalcboard.tutorial.step2_desc: Drag from Boiler's [Steam] output port (green) and drop onto empty canvas! Click [?] on the 4-button marker and select [Steam Turbine] to auto-wire.
gui.gtcalcboard.tutorial.step3_desc: [Double-Click] any existing connection wire! A zero-cost [↔ Reroute Junction Node] will instantly split and organize your wiring network.
gui.gtcalcboard.tutorial.step4_desc: First, [Right-Click] the connection wire to cut it! Then hold [Shift] while dragging from the junction output to the turbine input: the turbine count will automatically scale to 5.0x to match the 500 mB/s steam supply.
gui.gtcalcboard.tutorial.step5_junction_: [Left-Click] the bottom badge on the junction node to enter a target batch quantity (e.g. 1000 mB)! The estimated completion time (ET: 2.0s) calculates in real time based on steam inflow (500 mB/s). [Shift+Right-Click] to reset.
gui.gtcalcboard.tutorial.step5_selector_: Click the [Machine Icon] at the top-left of the node to open the machine selector. Inspect the capability badges (Coil, Parallel Hatch, Rotor, etc.) and select the [Electric Blast Furnace] multiblock!
gui.gtcalcboard.tutorial.step5_desc: Click the [⚙] config button on the turbine card! You can freely configure voltage tiers (LV~MAX), overclocking, coils, parallel hatches, and augment kits.
gui.gtcalcboard.tutorial.step6_desc: Drag-select both the Boiler and Turbine nodes, then press [Ctrl + G]! A clean [Group Frame] will wrap them, allowing batch moving and [✦] theme color styling.
gui.gtcalcboard.tutorial.step7_desc: Click the [▦] button on the frame header to compress the factory into a clean [Compound Module]! Click [⤢ Expand] anytime to restore the original wiring 100%.
gui.gtcalcboard.tutorial.step8_desc: Select the 3 geode slicing cutter nodes and press [Ctrl + Shift + S]! The 3 fractional cutter workloads merge into a single physical LV Cutter (45.0% load) with accurate single-machine power.
gui.gtcalcboard.tutorial.step9_desc: Click [▦ BOM] in the bottom status bar or press [Shift + B] / [M] to open the Multiblock BOM! Notice how the cutter hull and casings are counted exactly once for 1 machine instead of 3x duplicate hulls.
gui.gtcalcboard.tutorial.step10_desc: [Right-Click] the junction to open supply settings (or click [⚙ Configure Junction] in the right Inspector), then select [Infinite Supply (∞)] or [Fixed Rate]! This blocks upstream demand propagation, calculates stock Depletion Time (DT), or voids surplus byproducts.
gui.gtcalcboard.tutorial.step11_desc: Click the [📁] button on the left activity dock, [Page Name ▼] in the top toolbar, or press [Tab] to open the Folder Browser! Create nested subfolders, multi-select with Ctrl/Shift, drag & drop pages, and export/import full folder blueprints (GTFOLDER:...).
gui.gtcalcboard.tutorial.completed_desc: Congratulations! You are now ready to design massive petrochemical, nuclear, and multi-tier GregTech factories! Revisit [Help] or [Tutorial] anytime.
